audit.why: 47.15% over 1107 games. TRICKY at 7/10 with Annie carry threat 7.5/10 matches a losing win rate; the rating stayed and the chart was brought to it instead of the other way round.

audit.whatIsWrong: This is the packet's own listed defect: Akshan wins 47.15% but every one of the seven content rows said Akshan, and all seven whys argued Akshan. The full layer disagreed with all of it — phases[4].side and phases[6].side already read Annie while the rest read Skill, so the page rendered two different answers to who wins level 6.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row. Akshan genuinely owns levels 1-3 on the 850-vs-625 range gap, but Annie owns level 6 onward: Summon: Tibbers plus a stocked Pyromania is a point-and-click kill that needs no skillshot.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie across both layers, with whys[3..6] rewritten to argue the row they now sit on.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two outright errors about Pyromania. The page said the stun 'requires four spell-hits' — Riot says four CASTS, which she can stack on the minion wave without touching you. And it framed level 1 as safe: Riot's text says 'Annie begins the game and respawns with Pyromania available', so she has a stun ready at level 1 and again out of every respawn. Molten Shield was never mentioned at all, despite damaging enemies who strike her with attacks or spells — which is exactly what a three-hit Akshan string does. Disintegrate refunding its mana on a kill (so she never runs dry farming) was also absent.
audit.why: Riot text, enemy P: 'After casting 4 spells... Annie begins the game and respawns with Pyromania available.' Enemy E: 'damages enemies who strike her with attacks or spells.' Enemy Q: 'refunding the Mana cost if it destroys the target.'

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number anywhere, and the cooldown block was the generic 'budget E for emergencies' template.
audit.why: Disintegrate 4s flat, Incinerate 7s flat, Molten Shield 10s flat, Summon: Tibbers 130/115/100, Heroic Swing 18 at rank 1, Comeuppance 100/85/70. Tibbers at 130s is the one long window in her kit and it is the only safe time to contest her.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, ahead and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: late claimed 'this matchup only gets safer for you as the game goes on' — the opposite of a 47% win rate and of Annie's scaling.
audit.why: A point-and-click stun on a 100s ultimate does not get worse with items; Comeuppance's 2500 range is real but it stops on the first minion, so it is not the answer the page treated it as.

edits.before: Akshan holds a strong lane advantage since Annie is a short-range mage who must land multiple spells to charge her passive stun, while your Q boomerang lets you poke from further away without ever entering her threat range. Play around her mana and cooldowns, punishing her whenever she's used Disintegrate or Incinerate to farm. Watch for her stacking passive silently — if she gets four hits off you're vulnerable to a full combo, so back off once she's close to the stun threshold.
edits.after: Akshan holds an early advantage since Annie is a 625-range mage who must spend four spell casts to charge Pyromania, while your 850 boomerang lets you poke from outside her threat range entirely. Play around her mana and cooldowns, but remember Disintegrate refunds its cost when it kills a minion, so she farms for free. The stun is four casts, not four hits, and she respawns with Pyromania already stocked, so assume it is up unless you counted it spent.

edits.before: Once Annie hits 6, Tibbers turns her into a real all-in threat that can burst you down if her stun lands, so respect her combo windows and don't stand still in minion waves. Akshan's camouflage and E swing let you reposition out of her stun range before she commits, and you should keep poking from max range to deny her the free passive stacks she needs. She's forced into all-or-nothing engages, so patience wins this lane for you.
edits.after: Once Annie hits 6, Tibbers turns her into a real all-in threat that can burst you down if her stun lands, so respect her combo windows and don't stand still in minion waves. Akshan's camouflage and Heroic Swing reposition you out of her 600-range window, but Molten Shield is a 10s shield that burns anyone attacking her, so a full string into it trades badly. She engages all-or-nothing, so make her spend Pyromania on the wave first.

edits.before: With your first item completed you continue to out-poke her safely, since she still needs to walk up and land a full combo while you can hit her from range without retaliation. By two items your R threatens to execute her from well outside her Tibbers radius, meaning she has to play extremely passively or risk losing her ultimate for nothing — this matchup only gets safer for you as the game goes on.
edits.after: With your first item completed you continue to out-poke her safely, since she still needs to walk up and land a full combo while you can hit her from range without retaliation. By two items Comeuppance threatens her from 2500, well outside her 600 Tibbers radius, but one point-and-click Pyromania stun still ends you, so never take a fight where she can reach you without a wall to swing off first.

notes: The packet's flagged defect was real and is the main repair here: a 47.15% matchup was showing Akshan winning all seven stages while the full layer already said Annie at level 6 and 2+ items. I set the chart to Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie in both layers. Two things I could not resolve from the kits and did not assert: whether Tibbers counts as a 'minion' for Comeuppance's first-thing-hit rule (it would matter a lot — Tibbers standing between you and Annie would eat the shot), and whether Tibbers can knock Akshan off Heroic Swing under the 'colliding with champions' clause. Both are in questionsForUser.
